metadata.audience: English-speaking independent visitors interested in technology, design, modern China and the Greater Bay Area, 1–3 days
metadata.promise: Shenzhen technology travel is a way to read how hardware, supply chains, interfaces, city infrastructure and everyday consumption meet. It is not a fake factory tour.
metadata.commercial_boundary: Research and human-checked digital roadbook only. No company access, factory access, meetings, bookings, bundled travel, guiding or third-party experience sales.

source_policy.rule: Company access, exhibitions, transport, operating hours, market conditions and payments are dynamic. Use official venue/company/public-service sources and a dated human check; community posts only identify demand and friction.

research_basis.title: Community evidence: company factory access is usually restricted
research_basis.use: customer-expectation and refusal design, not operational authority

modules.name: What a Shenzhen tech trip actually is
modules.question: What are you trying to understand: hardware, consumer tech, manufacturing, AI, EVs, city systems or start-up culture?
modules.output_rule: Translate the vague word 'tech' into a learning question before selecting places.

modules.name: Huaqiangbei: supply-chain observation, not a bargain hunt
modules.question: How do I explore an electronics market without being misled about prices, quality or sourcing access?
modules.output_rule: Use a safety and observation protocol; do not promise bargains, warranties, authenticity or export support.

modules.name: Public-facing technology and city interfaces
modules.question: Where can I see technology as part of daily urban life rather than a corporate visit?
modules.output_rule: Use public retail/showroom/transport/urban-interface observations only after current access verification.

modules.name: Design, creative reuse and making
modules.question: What balances the hardware ecosystem with design and cultural production?
modules.output_rule: Use OCT Loft / design candidates as programme-dependent, not as a fixed exhibition list.

modules.name: Nanshan and the innovation-city landscape
modules.question: How do I understand Shenzhen's growth without a campus tour?
modules.output_rule: Use public waterfront, civic, retail and city-scale routes; never claim access to a company campus.

modules.name: Nantou and layered urban change
modules.question: Is there historical or lived texture inside a future-city trip?
modules.output_rule: Use public streets and adaptive-reuse discussion; do not call it a preserved 'authentic village' or enter private space.

modules.name: Hong Kong / Guangzhou / airport decision
modules.question: Is Shenzhen the destination, a Greater Bay Area connector, or a final technology chapter?
modules.output_rule: Ask border/visa eligibility, night count and true purpose; no cross-border or live-ticket promises.

modules.name: Tech-trip ethics and operational friction
modules.question: How do I avoid turning Shenzhen into corporate tourism theatre?
modules.output_rule: State factory-access limits, photography/IP etiquette, market risk, device/payment/data needs and human escalation.

points.name: Technology intent interview
points.why_it_matters: 'Tech' can mean consumer gadgets, sourcing, manufacturing systems, mobility, AI, design or curiosity about modern China. A good Shenzhen plan starts by separating these needs.
points.agent_use: Ask a learning question and desired depth before naming sites.

points.name: Huaqiangbei observation walk
points.why_it_matters: A visible interface to components, repair, retail, accessories and the density of a hardware ecosystem; strongest for observation rather than purchasing.
points.agent_use: Provide an observation brief, compare-before-buy rule and photography etiquette. Do not validate sellers or prices.

points.name: Huaqiangbei buying decision
points.why_it_matters: Buying a cheap accessory is different from sourcing parts, buying devices or trusting warranty claims.
points.agent_use: Ask whether purchase is actually needed. For anything material, recommend independent due diligence, not agent advice.

points.name: Public flagship/showroom decision
points.why_it_matters: Public retail or showrooms can help a visitor see how Chinese technology is presented to consumers, but are not factory or engineering access.
points.agent_use: Verify a current public-facing location and state exactly what it is; never imply an enterprise visit.

points.name: Shenzhen Science Museum / exhibition decision
points.why_it_matters: A possible public learning layer for science/technology visitors, contingent on current exhibitions, language and access.
points.agent_use: No recommendation until a current programme audit exists.

points.name: Metro, delivery and payment as urban interface
points.why_it_matters: For many visitors, the most legible technology is the public interface: transit, payments, maps and platform-mediated urban services.
points.agent_use: Use a real first-day setup audit and current public guidance; do not guarantee any app/payment method.

points.name: OCT Loft design/programme decision
points.why_it_matters: A counterweight to markets and malls: a possible lens on creative reuse, design and exhibition culture.
points.agent_use: Include only after checking the programme and reason it fits the client.

points.name: Maker/design workshop lead
points.why_it_matters: Potential later B2B or local-experience layer, but no workshops or access are sellable until participant safety, language, consent and commercial release are field-verified.
points.agent_use: Capture interest only; do not quote, book or imply availability.

points.name: Shenzhen Bay / Talent Park public realm
points.why_it_matters: A public-scale way to read the growth of Nanshan and the bay: skyline, mobility, waterfront and how innovation branding appears in civic space.
points.agent_use: Use public access only, build weather exits and do not imply campus access.

points.name: Nanshan retail/design decision
points.why_it_matters: A useful consumer-tech and design layer if the visitor wants to see devices, brands and contemporary retail—not a mandatory shopping stop.
points.agent_use: Clarify whether the goal is product observation, purchase or city atmosphere.

points.name: Nantou Ancient City public-street decision
points.why_it_matters: A route for discussing how a new city holds older urban fabric, restoration and commercial adaptation alongside the innovation narrative.
points.agent_use: Present it as layered change, not a timeless village. Keep to public streets and respectful observation.

points.name: Shekou / port-city decision
points.why_it_matters: A research candidate for port, migration, sea-facing urban life and a different social geography from Nanshan tech spaces.
points.agent_use: Hold until a field walk establishes a non-generic reason and responsible route.

points.name: One-day Shenzhen tech core
points.why_it_matters: A credible single-day structure is one hardware-market observation block plus one public innovation/design/city layer, with recovery time.
points.agent_use: Do not promise comprehensive Shenzhen in a day.

points.name: Two-day Shenzhen depth
points.why_it_matters: Adds a design or layered-city day so Shenzhen does not become a market-only trip.
points.agent_use: Use Day 2 only when the visitor has a genuine interest beyond buying gadgets.

points.name: Factory/campus request refusal and redirect
points.why_it_matters: Ordinary tourists should not be led to expect access to factories, R&D campuses, supply-chain facilities or private company meetings.
points.agent_use: State the boundary early. Redirect to legal public-facing market, showroom, museum and city-interface observation.

points.name: Market/IP/photography protocol
points.why_it_matters: Markets and companies require an ethics and safety layer: ask before photographing, do not obstruct work, do not infer supplier relationships and do not buy regulated/counterfeit goods.
points.agent_use: Include as explicit guest conduct, not hidden fine print.

points.name: Guangzhou–Shenzhen contrast card
points.why_it_matters: Guangzhou is food, trade history and Lingnan layers; Shenzhen is hardware ecosystem, innovation-city landscape and contemporary interfaces.
points.agent_use: Ask which city has the core purpose. Produce two roadbooks with handoff, not a saleable bundle.

points.name: Shenzhen–Hong Kong border decision
points.why_it_matters: A border crossing is not a casual metro extension: it can alter immigration/visa eligibility, payment, data, luggage and usable hours.
points.agent_use: Require the client's passport/visa and current official confirmation; no generic border advice.

points.name: Arrival / airport departure risk
points.why_it_matters: Shenzhen is often placed at the end of a journey; flight-day plans must distinguish a real day from an anxious transfer window.
points.agent_use: Ask departure airport/time and luggage handling before recommending any final-day activity.

points.name: Tech-trip commercial boundary
points.why_it_matters: The product's credibility depends on stating what it is: independent research, a route and a human check—not access brokerage or sourcing consultancy.
points.agent_use: Use this boundary when a visitor asks for suppliers, factory introductions, purchase protection or private access.

follow_up_questions.ask: What do you actually want to understand: hardware, consumer products, making, AI/EVs, city infrastructure, design or business?
Are you observing, buying a small personal item, sourcing for a business, or photographing the ecosystem?
Are you seeking public learning, a commercial supplier relationship, or a private company visit? The last two require a separate, non-travel scope.
Do you prefer creative reuse, architecture, waterfront public realm or a layered old-city contrast?
What passport/visa status applies, and do you have an official current basis for the border crossing?
Is Guangzhou needed for food/trade history and Shenzhen for technology, and how many true nights can you give each?
Which airport, what departure time, and will you have luggage on your final day?
Would you like a human-checked research brief with official links, while you make all bookings directly?

output_guardrails: Never promise factory, R&D campus, supplier, company meeting or private workshop access.
Never state an electronics product is genuine, safe, exportable, compatible, warrantied or a bargain.
Never present Huaqiangbei as a shopping trick; it is a responsible observation/product-risk decision.
Never name current exhibitions, public showrooms or venue access without dated verification.
Never give generic Hong Kong border/visa advice; use an official and traveller-specific human-check gate.
No sourcing brokerage, booking, payment collection, bundling, guiding or third-party experience sales.
